```{r setup}
res_dir <- "results"
need <- function(f) {
  p <- file.path(res_dir, f)
  if (!file.exists(p)) stop("Missing ", p, ". Run: Rscript run_experiment.R --main", call. = FALSE)
  utils::read.csv(p, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
}
summary <- need("summary.csv")
truths <- need("truths.csv")
meta <- need("metadata.csv")
est_levels <- c(ipw = "IPW", pairwise = "Pairwise", cat_fiml = "Saturated cat-FIML",
                ds_fiml = "DS-FIML", loglin2_fiml = "Log-linear (all-2-way) FIML",
                nt_fiml = "NT-FIML")
lab <- function(e) ifelse(e %in% names(est_levels), est_levels[e], e)
```

## Question

nt-fiml is consistent under MCAR for any distribution and efficient under MAR
when normality holds, because the Gaussian is saturated in exactly the moments
quadratic kappa needs (means + covariances) and max-entropy beyond. For
nominal-weight Conger/Fleiss — which depend only on the univariate and bivariate
margins of the rating distribution — the discrete analogue is the
**all-2-way-interaction log-linear model** (the maximum-entropy distribution
matching all 1-way and 2-way margins). Does it inherit nt-fiml's duality:
model-free consistency under MCAR, and consistency + efficiency under MAR when
the truth has no genuine 3-way-or-higher rater interactions?

DS-FIML, by contrast, constrains the 2-way margins through a latent class, so it
is *not* expected to be model-free MCAR-consistent — it carries a misspecification
bias asymptote ([[project_ds_fiml_prototype]]). The contrast is the headline.

## Short answer

```{r answer, results = "asis"}
# Filled narratively below from the evidence tables.
cat("The duality holds (the bias-vs-n contrast H1 and the MAR tables H2/H3), ",
    "and the new delta-method SEs are well calibrated (H4): by n >= 400, ",
    "`SE/SD` ~ 1 and coverage ~0.95 in every cell -- including under MAR, where ",
    "the MCAR-only IPW interval instead collapses.\n", sep = "")
```

## H1 — MCAR model-free consistency (3-way-interaction truth `ds_4x4`)

On a Dawid–Skene severity truth (genuine higher-order rater interactions), under
MCAR: does each estimator's bias vanish as n grows? The log-linear FIML and the
saturated cat-FIML should → 0 (they preserve the 2-way margins); DS-FIML should
plateau at its misspecification asymptote.

```{r h1-table}
h1 <- summary[summary$dgp == "ds_4x4" & summary$mechanism == "mcar30" &
                summary$weight == "nominal" & summary$coefficient == "Conger", ]
h1 <- h1[order(h1$estimator, h1$n), c("estimator", "n", "bias", "sd", "rmse")]
h1$estimator <- lab(h1$estimator)
knitr::kable(h1, digits = 4, row.names = FALSE,
             col.names = c("Estimator", "n", "Bias", "SD", "RMSE"))
```

```{r h1-plot, fig.width = 7, fig.height = 4.2}
op <- par(mar = c(4, 4, 1, 1))
ests <- unique(h1$estimator)
cols <- seq_along(ests)
ns <- sort(unique(h1$n))
plot(NA, xlim = range(ns), ylim = range(c(0, h1$bias)), log = "x",
     xlab = "n (log scale)", ylab = "Bias (Conger, nominal)")
abline(h = 0, col = "grey60", lty = 2)
for (i in seq_along(ests)) {
  d <- h1[h1$estimator == ests[i], ]
  lines(d$n, d$bias, type = "b", col = cols[i], pch = 19)
}
legend("topright", legend = ests, col = cols, pch = 19, lty = 1, bty = "n", cex = 0.85)
par(op)
```

## H2 — MAR efficiency when the restriction holds (`loglin2_4x4`)

On an all-2-way truth (the restriction holds exactly), under MAR: the log-linear
FIML should be consistent and lower-RMSE than the MCAR-only baselines (IPW),
which are MAR-biased.

```{r h2-table}
h2 <- summary[summary$dgp == "loglin2_4x4" & summary$mechanism == "mar_anchor30" &
                summary$weight == "nominal" & summary$coefficient == "Conger", ]
h2 <- h2[order(h2$estimator, h2$n), c("estimator", "n", "bias", "sd", "rmse")]
h2$estimator <- lab(h2$estimator)
knitr::kable(h2, digits = 4, row.names = FALSE,
             col.names = c("Estimator", "n", "Bias", "SD", "RMSE"))
```

## H3 — MAR robustness boundary (3-way-interaction truth `ds_4x4`)

On the interaction-bearing truth under MAR, no estimator's working model is
correct; characterise the residual bias of each rung.

```{r h3-table}
h3 <- summary[summary$dgp == "ds_4x4" & summary$mechanism == "mar_anchor30" &
                summary$weight == "nominal" & summary$coefficient == "Conger", ]
h3 <- h3[order(h3$estimator, h3$n), c("estimator", "n", "bias", "sd", "rmse")]
h3$estimator <- lab(h3$estimator)
knitr::kable(h3, digits = 4, row.names = FALSE,
             col.names = c("Estimator", "n", "Bias", "SD", "RMSE"))
```

## H4 — Standard-error calibration (log-linear FIML)

The C++ `estimate_kappa_loglin2` carries delta-method SEs: the Louis observed
information in the model's sufficient-statistic (1-way + 2-way margin)
coordinates, mapped through the implied-kappa Jacobian. Two diagnostics below:
`SE/SD` (mean delta-method SE over the across-replication SD of the estimate —
pure SE calibration, target 1) and Wald coverage about the **exact** truth
(which additionally absorbs any point bias).

```{r h4-loglin2}
h4 <- summary[summary$estimator == "loglin2_fiml" & summary$weight == "nominal" &
                summary$coefficient == "Conger", ]
h4 <- h4[order(h4$dgp, h4$mechanism, h4$n),
         c("dgp", "mechanism", "n", "bias", "sd", "mean_se", "se_sd", "coverage")]
knitr::kable(h4, digits = c(0, 0, 0, 4, 4, 4, 3, 3), row.names = FALSE,
             col.names = c("DGP", "Mechanism", "n", "Bias", "SD", "Mean SE",
                           "SE/SD", "Cover"))
```

The SE is well calibrated wherever loglin2 is consistent. By n ≥ 400 `SE/SD`
sits in 0.96–1.05 and coverage in 0.94–0.96 in *every* cell — including the
`ds_4x4` MAR boundary, where loglin2's residual fill-in bias turns out to be
tiny (Conger bias −0.003 at n = 1600), so coverage recovers to nominal rather
than collapsing. The only sub-nominal coverage is at n = 40 (0.81–0.92): partly
small-n FIML point bias, and under anchor-MAR partly an SE optimism of ~20%
(`SE/SD` ≈ 0.79) — the same n ≤ 40 weak spot the other FIMLs show. It clears by
n ≥ 100–400.

### Coverage across estimators (largest n)

```{r h4-cross}
cross <- summary[summary$n == max(summary$n) & summary$weight == "nominal" &
                   summary$coefficient == "Conger" & is.finite(summary$coverage), ]
cross <- cross[order(cross$dgp, cross$mechanism, cross$estimator),
               c("dgp", "mechanism", "estimator", "se_sd", "coverage")]
cross$estimator <- lab(cross$estimator)
knitr::kable(cross, digits = 3, row.names = FALSE,
             col.names = c("DGP", "Mechanism", "Estimator", "SE/SD", "Cover"))
```

At n = 1600 the contrast with the MCAR-only baseline is sharp: under anchor-MAR,
log-linear FIML and saturated cat-FIML hold nominal coverage (~0.95) while IPW
collapses (0.65 on `ds_4x4`, 0.90 on `loglin2_4x4`) — its `SE/SD` is ~1, so this
is bias, not a variance miss: the IPW interval is centred on the MAR-biased
estimand. The log-linear FIML interval is valid under MAR; IPW's is not.

## Ladder summary

```{r ladder}
big <- summary[summary$n == max(summary$n) & summary$coefficient == "Conger" &
                 summary$weight == "nominal", ]
big <- big[order(big$dgp, big$mechanism, big$estimator),
           c("dgp", "mechanism", "estimator", "bias", "rmse")]
big$estimator <- lab(big$estimator)
knitr::kable(big, digits = 4, row.names = FALSE,
             col.names = c("DGP", "Mechanism", "Estimator", "Bias", "RMSE"))
```

## Caveats

- `loglin2_fiml` here is the C++ `estimate_kappa_loglin2` (it matches the R EM
  prototype in `R/loglin2_fiml.R` to ~1e-5 and runs in milliseconds rather than
  seconds); the R EM is retained only for the closed-form truth helpers. The
  full `C^R` table is still materialised, so the simulation stays at `C=4, R=4`
  (the `ds_5x6` cell is ~2 min/fit and excluded).
- Coverage is computed about the *exact* truth, so it absorbs point bias; the
  `SE/SD` column isolates SE calibration. Low coverage with `SE/SD` ~ 1 (the H3
  MAR boundary, or small n) is a bias effect, not an SE defect.
- `ds_fiml` is carried point-only (NA SE columns) — its delta-method SEs are
  validated separately in workbench 37.
- All estimators target the same fixed-rater estimand; truth is exact from each
  DGP's generating margins.

## Reproduce

```{r repro, results = "asis"}
cat(sprintf("Seed base %s, %s reps/cell, run %s.\n\n", meta$seed_base, meta$reps, meta$timestamp))
```

```sh
Rscript run_experiment.R --main --reps 500
```
